# quantity value

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:quantityValue`](gmeow-quantityValue.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/quantityValue>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/observations`](../../slices/observations.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The numeric value of a scalar quantity, as an [xsd:decimal.](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal.) Functional: a scalar quantity has exactly one numeric value. Meaningful only with its unit ([`gmeow:hasUnit`](gmeow-hasUnit.md)) — no silent units.

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; [`gmeow:ScalarQuantity`](../classes/gmeow-ScalarQuantity.md) -> [`xsd:decimal`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:quantityValue`](gmeow-quantityValue.md) from [`gmeow:ScalarQuantity`](../classes/gmeow-ScalarQuantity.md) to [`xsd:decimal`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

### Temperature Reading

- **Source:** [`slices/core/observations/examples/temperature-reading.ttl`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/slices/core/observations/examples/temperature-reading.ttl)
- **Examples catalog:** [open in catalog](../../examples/index.md#example-slices-core-observations-examples-temperature-reading)#example-slices-core-observations-examples-temperature-reading

```turtle
# --- The result wrapper: value + unit + uncertainty, not a bare literal.
ex:temp a gmeow:ScalarQuantity ;
    gmeow:quantityValue       "22.5"^^xsd:decimal ;
    gmeow:quantityUncertainty "0.1"^^xsd:decimal ;
    gmeow:hasUnit             <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG_C> .
```

### Spatial Bins

- **Source:** [`slices/extensions/aggregation/examples/spatial-bins.ttl`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/slices/extensions/aggregation/examples/spatial-bins.ttl)
- **Examples catalog:** [open in catalog](../../examples/index.md#example-slices-extensions-aggregation-examples-spatial-bins)#example-slices-extensions-aggregation-examples-spatial-bins

```turtle
# The result is a scalar with its unit (a Quantity must declare exactly one unit,
# P11); a count of persons-per-household is the dimensionless QUDT number unit.
ex:avgHouseholdSize a gmeow:ScalarQuantity ;
    gmeow:quantityValue "2.4"^^xsd:decimal ;
    gmeow:hasUnit       <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/NUM> .
```

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to carry the bare numeric magnitude of a [`gmeow:ScalarQuantity`](../classes/gmeow-ScalarQuantity.md) (or its aliases) — the literal that, paired with [`gmeow:hasUnit`](gmeow-hasUnit.md), makes the reading meaningful.

### Avoid when

- Avoid publishing or comparing it without its [`gmeow:hasUnit`](gmeow-hasUnit.md) (no silent units), avoid it for money (use [`gmeow:monetaryValue`](gmeow-monetaryValue.md), whose currency frame is required), and avoid asserting two values — it is functional.

### How to use

- Put the magnitude here as [xsd:decimal](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal), name the unit with [`gmeow:hasUnit`](gmeow-hasUnit.md), the spread with [`gmeow:quantityUncertainty`](gmeow-quantityUncertainty.md), and the ontic model with [`gmeow:hasDeterminacy`](gmeow-hasDeterminacy.md); consumers read magnitude and unit together.

### Examples

- ex:temp22 [`gmeow:quantityValue`](gmeow-quantityValue.md) 22.5.
